BABEL
VISUAL STORY · 1 / 4

Humanity gathered at Babel.

One people. One place. One project. “Let us make a name for ourselves.”

WHAT YOU JUST SAW

The Bible just made a major turn.

Genesis begins by looking broadly at humanity. After Babel, the story narrows to one man and his family, but God’s purpose still reaches outward.

01 · BABELHumanity gathers.One place. One project.
02 · SCATTEREDThe people spread.Many places and peoples.
03 · ABRAHAMGod calls one man.One family carries the promise.
04 · NATIONSThe purpose stays global.Blessing reaches all families.
Keep this: The story narrows to one family without shrinking God’s purpose for the world.
THE PROMISE · GENESIS 12

God calls Abram and gives him something to trust.

God tells Abram to leave his country and go to a land He will show him. The promise can be remembered with three handles: Land. Seed. Blessing.

TAP REVEAL

Next: The promise has been spoken. But Abraham still has no child. That tension takes us to Genesis 15.
GENESIS 15 · TRUST BEFORE SIGHT

Years pass. Abraham still has no child.

Abraham brings that problem before God. God takes him outside, points him to the stars, and tells him that his descendants will be beyond what he can presently see.

What changed? Nothing visible yet. But Abraham believed God. The promise is now moving from words toward a family.
Before we meet Isaac, hold onto the tension.Abraham has a promise, but still no son. The next part of the story is where waiting finally becomes fulfillment.
THE FAMILY · FROM ABRAHAM TO ISRAEL

The promise becomes a family.

Abraham had no son, and he brought that ache honestly to God. God answered by taking him beneath the stars and promising descendants beyond what Abraham could count or see.

Then the promised son finally came. Isaac was born when Abraham was 100 years old and Sarah was 90. Isaac is not a random new character; he is the visible arrival of the promise Abraham and Sarah had waited to receive.

is not only a happy family moment. It teaches students that the promise depends on God’s faithfulness before it becomes a genealogy to memorize.

Isaac has a son named Jacob. God later renames Jacob Israel. Israel has twelve sons, whose families become the tribes of Israel.

ABRAHAMthe man God called
ISAACthe promised son born after waiting
JACOB → ISRAELIsrael was a person before Israel was a people
TWELVE SONSthe family grows
Now the next question: How did this family end up in Egypt?
This is where Joseph matters.We are summarizing a long story, but the road is clear: jealousy → betrayal → Egypt → slavery → authority → famine → family preserved.
JOSEPH · WHY EGYPT?

Joseph explains the move.

Joseph was one of Jacob’s sons, and his brothers hated him. Their jealousy became betrayal: they sold him to traders who were going down to Egypt. Joseph arrived there as a slave, far from home and far from the family story he knew.

But Joseph’s story did not end as a slave. Through suffering, faithfulness, and God’s care, Joseph eventually rose into authority in Egypt. When came, his position became the way Jacob’s family survived and came to live in Egypt.

JACOB / ISRAEL
TWELVE SONS
JOSEPH → EGYPT
THE FAMILY MOVES TO EGYPT

CONNECTION COMPLETE

You connected one promise across Scripture.

Genesis 3 introduces the promised Seed. Genesis 12 narrows the line to Abraham. Genesis 22 keeps the nations in view. Galatians later looks back and connects the Abrahamic promise to Christ.

CONNECT · WEEK 03 REVIEW

What you just connected.

You traced one developing promise across Scripture. Here is the connection you just uncovered.

GEN 3:15→GEN 12:1–3→GEN 22:18→GAL 3:16→CHRIST
GENESIS 3:15

Seed Promised

After the Fall, Scripture introduces the expectation of a coming offspring. The serpent will not have the final word.

GENESIS 12:1–3

Abraham Called

The promise narrows to one man and one family, while God’s purpose still reaches all families of the earth.

GENESIS 22:18

Nations Blessed

The offspring promise and the blessing of the nations remain connected.

GALATIANS 3:16

Paul Looks Back

The New Testament reaches back to Abraham’s offspring promise and relates its climactic fulfillment to Christ.

THE BIG CONNECTION

The promise becomes more specific as Scripture unfolds, but it never becomes smaller. It moves toward Christ while keeping the nations in view.
